name: Alliant Energy Foundation Community Grants
summary: Corporate foundation community grants in Alliant Energy service communities; one of three focus areas is environmental stewardship, including tree and prairie planting and habitat restoration.

eligibility.rule: Is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit, public school, government entity or tax-exempt organization
Receives at most one grant per calendar year
Does not propose political activity, directly or indirectly
Does not propose an energy-related project
If faith-promoting, has a separate 501c3 and a secular project
Does not discriminate on the listed protected grounds
Is not an animal welfare agency or animal training service

calls.label: Three review cycles a year
calls.recurring: Deadlines to apply each year: January 15, May 15 and September 15.

status.quote: We accept applications year-round and review them three times a year.

recurring.quote: Application schedule grant cycle deadline to apply grants awarded Cycle one January 15 April 1 Cycle two May 15 August 1 Cycle three September 15 December 1

applicant_types.quote: Funds are only available for 501(c)(3) nonprofit organizations, public schools, government entities and tax-exempt organizations located within the communities Alliant Energy serves.

geography.quote: Funds are only available for 501(c)(3) nonprofit organizations, public schools, government entities and tax-exempt organizations located within the communities Alliant Energy serves.

access.quote: We manage applications for Alliant Energy's Community Grants through our CyberGrants portal.

window.quote: We have one application and three deadlines throughout the year.

effort.quote: We manage applications for Alliant Energy's Community Grants through our CyberGrants portal.

eligibility.quote: Funds are only available for 501(c)(3) nonprofit organizations, public schools, government entities and tax-exempt organizations
Organizations are eligible for one grant per calendar year.
Support of political activity, either directly or indirectly.
Energy-related projects, including solar panels, generators, lighting, heating, electric vehicle charging stations or other items related to Alliant Energy's core business.
Religious institutions or other organizations promoting faith unless they have a 501c3 separate from the church and the project is secular.
Organizations that discriminate against people because of their age, race, creed, gender identity, disability, sexual orientation, ethnicity or national origin.
Animal welfare agencies or animal training services.
